title: Phishing, social engineering and ransomware on the corporate network

videos.script: The most successful attack on a company network does not break anything. It asks. A message, a link, a document, a person who opens it. {{ask}} The firewall was right to let it in. So this lesson is about everything that happens next, and where the network can make it stop. {{stages}} A name server that refuses to resolve a reported phishing page, and remembers who asked. {{dns}} Workstations that stop answering each other, because they never needed to. {{lateral}} A machine cut off from the network with one line, while its neighbours carry on. {{quarantine}} And backups built so that an infected machine cannot reach them at all. {{backup}}
